text: I got this game at release, and despite my main interest being the co-op mode, I started by playing through it alone. I loved it. Its relocation mechanic makes for a very different kind of stealth, which really comes into its own with the wide open levels that are full of alternative paths, places to hide, and elevated sniper positions. The controls are responsive and the weapons are satisfying. Unfortunately the net code is atrocious. I have been unable to finish most of the levels in co-op because it randomly kicks me or my partner. Not even necessarily when something interesting happens, we'll be in the middle of doing something and the game kicks us both back to the main menu. In very long missions this can be a tremendous waste of time, as we can sometimes play for half an hour before we get kicked, and it won't let us wait for our partner to rejoin or even just load a savegame. "Maybe it's your connection", I hear you say. Nope, we were on Skype the whole time and the call never dropped. There are other issues in multiplayer. Sometimes when I start a game in co-op, I have no scope reticle (making sniping somewhat difficult). On one occasion, I was playing the Survival mode and we'd made it to the last round - my friend went down, and when I revived him, he got stuck in spectator mode. His character was just lying there uselessly looking around. If you want to play this game in singleplayer, buy it. It's a fairly long game - 9 missions including the tutorial, but each is easily an hour long, probably more. Worth the asking price for sure. If you're buying it for co-op, give it a miss. You probably won't be able to.

text: This game disappointed me, it has all the elements that could make a good sniper game like setting up ambushes, scoring headshots and even the cool kill-cam, but it's hampered by the other limitations this game has starting with the AI. The AI goes beyond the typical moronic stealth soldiers if that were even possible. A common tactic you would employ is to kill an entire squad run away from where they last see you and they completely forget you even exist. The AI wouldn't have been a problem if they took splinter cells' alarm system. As for the actual stealth it's what you would expect you sneak around and shoot people with a silenced pistol. You can also kick generators to cover up the sound of your sniper rifle, how this muffles the sound of a mosin-nagant I have no idea. All in all it was a dull and boring game to play through, it did run great though I guess that's a plus.

title: sniper elite: nazi zombie army
text: This game is really fun. The atmosphere is super creepy and desolate. The sounds of the environment to the sounds of your gun shooting is very nice and distinct. The funnest thing about the game was the different kind of zombies. -You've got your standard nazi zombie. He's very weak but always attacks you in large groups. -Then you've got skeletal zombies. These guys aren't much different then the standard zombie, however, they are immune to headshots and instead must be shot in the heart. There attack speed is slightly faster as well, but also do less damage then the standard zombies. -The 3rd class of zombie is a suicide grunt. This guy will rush towards the survivors at an eerily creepy speed. Once he reachers his target he then explodes violently, severely damaging anyone near him. -And then there's the heavy MG zombie. This zombie is a boss zombie. He can deal a massive amount of damage at short to medium range. He is also slightly immune to headshots. His head ,however, is his weakspot, and he can be brought down with consistent accurate headshots. -Now, the fifth zombie is a sniper zombie. These guys never directly engage the survivors. Instead they harrass the survivors from afar while jumping from building to building like a kangaroo right out of Austrailia. (Silly, I know) -Then for the final zombie you've got a giant phantasmal like entity. He is a boss zombie. His unique ability to summon the undead horde makes him the hardest to deal with. He also emits a shield that deflects all incoming bullets from the survivors. This shield can only be brought down by shooting the skulls that flost around this zombie. I had a blast playing this game just wish the game had more levels(only 5), but for 15 dollars one can not really complain.

title: sniper: ghost warrior
text: I kinda only have complains about this game: The graphics are not very good, even for the time when this game was released, the controls are kinda weird too, specially when your character is using an assault weapon instead of the sniper rifle, also there's no real consistency as to when the NPCs notice you when you're trying to sneak into camps, sometimes they do when you're actually hidden and sometimes you can pretty much walk past by then in plain sight when they should see you. You can't run very long unless you want your character to pretty much start having an asthma attack, same goes when you're trying to snipe, your character is breathing too hard and sometime you have to use the 'hold your breath' function to make a good shoot, I know this is supposed to give a realistic spin to the game play but it gets annoying after a while. The game does give you a chance to see special cutscenes when you make a clean headshot, but only for certain NPCs, not everytime you actually make the shot. Speaking of the NPCs, their conversations are always the same, always, there's never chance, and they sound weird because they were recorded by actors that are evidently spanish instead of latinamerican, which wouldn't be such a big deal if the game wasn't set in Latinamerican and the actor weren't so bad at changing their accent. But for all the complains I have, this game is kinda addictive, if only for the need of actually wanting to complete it more than anything else (there's no real story to follow), it helps that is relatively short, so if you have nothing better to play and you want to kill a couple of hours, you can try it.

title: snow
text: I don't normally review games, but SNOW has so much potential that i feel i have to give my feedback on it. First of all, it's a great idea, there's no other games like this and the free-roaming skiing premise has not been done very much before. Bearing in mind that it's completely free-to-play, i think it very good. It's still got many bugs, but as a free to play early access that only to be expected. There's a huge variety of maps, and the controls are relatively easy to get the hang of. However, the new update has caused my character to die whenever i get dropped off, meaning only snowboarding works as an option, which is very frustrating as skiing feels more fluid at the moment. Also, the charcter model has completely disappeared (if intentional this really detracts from the game), so my skier has is merely a floating hat and gloves, with no body. Would I recommend? Yes. its free, so why not? There are many bugs and it's certainly still in early stages, but there is huge potential here, and a finished product could be outstanding.

title: snow
text: Purchased this as it boasted VR Support and showed the Oculas Rift on its webpage. Unfortunatly this is a purchase I very much regret for now. WHile it looks and plays fine in 2D for an Alpha product, when you enable 3D via the Oculas Rift I found the game unplayable. This is the only time i've found the experience better in 2D than in 3D through the rift. General complaints are: Low Framerate (Even when all settings are set to low) Very Flat "3D" objects. Such as Trees and background. (Looks like a flat picture as the background) Distancing issue with objects (The moon appears about 4 meters away from your head and closer than other objects) Very sparse amount of 3D objects so you get a very poor 3D feel. View disorientating. (If your character is infront of your view. Head tracking does not work correctly) When in "First Person" any character movement affects your view. Overall I would not recommend this game for use with the Oculas Rift as its a disappointing experience. If this changes, im happy to update this review.
